summary: Build practical skills in Article 6 authorization, registry choices, reporting, and NDC alignment. Explore the five-day practitioner course.
lede: Paris Agreement Article 6 implementation turns cooperative-approach and mechanism rules into public-sector authorization, coordination, and reporting processes. Designed for climate officials, regulators, NDC coordinators, and government legal and reporting staff, the course helps develop workable host-Party arrangements. Participants practise setting authorization criteria, mapping agency responsibilities, assessing registry choices, and planning corresponding-adjustment and reporting workflows aligned with NDC implementation.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for public-sector and climate-finance professionals who shape, authorize, coordinate, or report Paris Agreement Article 6 activity. It suits practitioners who need to connect institutional decisions with NDC implementation and international reporting. This course is designed for: Climate ministry officials assigning Article 6 mandates across public agencies. Carbon-market regulators reviewing authorization criteria and activity eligibility. NDC coordination officers aligning Article 6 activity with national targets. Government climate lawyers drafting authorization procedures and host-Party arrangements. Climate reporting officers coordinating Article 6 information for transparency submissions. National registry administrators assessing tracking and account-management requirements. Climate-finance specialists screening cooperative approaches for public-sector implementation. Article 6 focal points preparing inter-agency decision records and workflows. Environmental policy advisers assessing Article 6.8 non-market approaches. Public-sector auditors reviewing authorization controls and corresponding-adjustment evidence.
prerequisites: Expected preparation: working familiarity with national climate policy, NDC processes, or public-sector climate governance. Prior experience with carbon-market project development or offset-project MRV is not required. No coding is required; participants should be able to work with basic digital documents and spreadsheets.
